# National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997 (NLSY97): agent index

BLS's panel survey of about 9,000 people born in 1980-84, interviewed annually from 1997 to 2011 and every two years since; managed by CHRR at The Ohio State University, interviews by NORC.

Publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS); produced and distributed by the Center for Human Resource Research (CHRR), The Ohio State University. Dataset id: `nlsy97`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.nlsinfo.org/content/getting-started/accessing-data. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the survey year.

## Releases

| Release | Table | Variables | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1997-2023` | person | 377 | NLSY97 cohort data, 1997-2023 (rounds 1-21) |
| `1997-2023` | person_year | 20 | NLSY97 cohort data, 1997-2023 (rounds 1-21) |

Tables in `1997-2023`: the key identifies a row; a reference says which columns join to another table, and when.

- `person`: One row per respondent: questions asked once, and the sample design. Key: PUBID
- `person_year`: One row per respondent and survey year (21 rows each). Key: PUBID, SURVEY_YEAR. References: PUBID -> person

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `1997-2023`: 1997-2011,2013,2015,2017,2019,2021,2023,XRND. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.
